description: One unit of work waiting to be handed to an agent: what it is, how long it is expected to take, how urgent it is and which agent holds it right now. The record is a VALUE: the host recomposes it with task with { … } when a task is renamed, re-estimated or assigned, and no component mutates the instance it was given. Id is the identity the board keys the assignment overlay on and the value every callback reports, so a blank id is REJECTED at construction — an id the model invented would change on every rebuild of the host's snapshot and silently move a task back to the backlog. Nothing is invented. A missing EstimatedDuration means "not estimated" (the board prints no duration and its occupied-until preview cannot project past the agent's own load), a zero or negative one is not an estimate either, a missing Priority is not Normal, and a blank or whitespace AssignedAgentId is the same as no assignment at all.

members.name: EstimatedDuration
members.description: How long the task is expected to take. Null (the default), Zero and a negative span all mean "not estimated": the board shows no duration line and never claims an end time it cannot compute.

members.name: HasEstimate
members.description: Whether the host gave the task a usable estimate.

members.name: HasKnownPriority
members.description: Whether Priority is one of the declared grades (a cast integer may not be).

members.name: HasPriority
members.description: Whether the host gave the task a priority.

members.name: Id
members.description: Stable identity of the task. Never empty: construction rejects a blank value.

members.name: IsAssignable
members.description: Whether the task is ready to be handed to somebody. A priority and an estimate are optional, so every task in the backlog is assignable; the flag exists so a surface can ask the question in the model's own terms.

members.name: IsAssigned
members.description: Whether an agent holds the task right now.

members.name: Priority
members.description: How urgent the task is. Null (the default) means the host has no priority for it, which renders no priority chip at all — an invented Normal would be a judgement nobody made.

members.name: Title
members.description: The task in the host's own words. A whitespace-only title reads as empty.
